newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Plane to retrieve American's body from Antarctic.
newsitem.headline: Plane to retrieve American's body from Antarctic.

text.p: A U.S. Navy spokesman said on Tuesday a rescue aircraft would attempt a rare winter landing at the United States' McMurdo Base in Antarctica to retrieve the body of an American man who died last week.
A U.S. Air Force Starlifter transport plane was scheduled to land on the Ross Ice Shelf to retrieve the body of contractor Charles Gallagher, who died of a heart problem.
He was the 48th American to perish in the Antarctic since 1955.
The U.S. Navy said the plane would take off at 6 a.m. on Wednesday (1800 GMT, Tuesday) from Christchurch on New Zealand's South Island and was scheduled to return that day.
The flight is unusual because cold, harsh weather and a lack of sunlight during the Antarctic winter usually isolate staff at McMurdo from March to August.
The plane would also take fresh food, mail and medical supplies for McMurdo and New Zealand's Scott Base.
The plane will land at the Pegasus field runway on the Ross Ice Shelf.
Antarctica saw the sun for the last time this winter two weeks ago but the frozen continent still experienced five hours of twilight during the middle of the day.
Temperatures last week dropped to minus 37 degrees Celsius (minus 34.6 Fahrenheit) with a wind-chill factor as low as minus 72 degrees Celsius (minus 97.6 Fahrenheit).
